title: Can Language Models Discover Scaling Laws?

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary discovery of scaling laws for foundation-model behavior
mechanism.populationDetail: Five persistent islands each maintain a population of 100 candidate programs, with migration every 25 generations.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The MAP-Elites database bins candidates by score, complexity, and diversity metrics.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The same evolutionary database provides island population memory and MAP-Elites quality-diversity organization; exact cell admission and eviction details are not exposed.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM modifies one selected parent program pair, potentially changing the law form, optimizer, or global variables; other programs are contextual inspirations.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Score is the primary objective signal, not additional evaluator metadata; complexity and diversity serve as archive descriptors.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Parent is selected from the database under fixed high-score/diversity/elite proportions; inspiration programs are additional context only.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The evolved individual is a coupled pair comprising a symbolic scaling-law expression and a parameter-fitting optimization routine.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/CAN LANGUAGE MODELS DISCOVER SCALING LAWS？.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The current manuscript calls EvoSLD's explore/exploit balance implicit, but Section 3 and Appendix D specify fixed 70/20/10 exploitation, exploration, and elitism proportions. QD archive admission/replacement and exact parent-sampling scope are incompletely specified.
